what: A RECORD OF WHAT GRADERS RETURNED. Not a claim about the renderer.
why_this_file_exists: Round one's result lived only in commit messages and in three prose volumes. Round two's lived nowhere in the tree at all, and two documentation volumes independently refused to cite it — correctly, because an uncitable number is not a result. This file is the durable record for both rounds, beside the pair manifests that produced them (tools/ab-pairs-round1.json, tools/ab-pairs-round2.json). A score in here is evidence about a deck; the finding under `limitation` is the reason a score in here is worth much less than it looks.
how_to_read_a_score_here: A round is three graders x fourteen pairs = 42 calls. Do not add rounds together into a single fraction: round one is 42/42 and round two is 42/42, which is 84/84 across both rounds, and '42/42 across both rounds' — which is how this was first handed over — halves the denominator.

rounds.protocol: one grader per pair, isolated context. Each saw exactly two images and a README, in a directory named by an unordered seeded token, with the pair number stripped from the filenames. No grader could see another pair or another grader.
rounds.why_the_protocol_changed: rounds 1 and 2 used one grader across all fourteen pairs, which is one trial and not fourteen: this engine has a single signature, so a grader who cracks any pair gets the rest on palette alone. Accuracy therefore reads 100% until it reads 50%, with no resolving power in between. Round 3 removes the thirteen free confirmations.
rounds.score: 14/14. Eleven calls at confidence 5, three at confidence 4, no 1s, 2s or 3s.

limitation.headline: A 14-pair deck drawn from a single engine is one trial, not fourteen.
limitation.detail: Our renderer has one signature — one grass, one helmet, one sky model, one tone curve. A grader who cracks any single pair gets the rest on palette alone, so the fourteen calls are not fourteen independent observations. Accuracy therefore reads 100% until it reads 50%, with no usable range in between, and the instrument has no resolving power precisely in the region where progress happens. Round two is the demonstration: six of eight statistics closed, the edge gap by 82%, and the score moved not at all.
limitation.consequence: Neither 42/42 is evidence about the size of the remaining gap. Both are evidence that the gap is not yet zero, which is all a saturated instrument can say.

proposal_not_implemented.status: PROPOSAL. Not implemented at 3f4c203. Do not cite this as protocol.
proposal_not_implemented.shape: One pair per grader, in a fresh context. That restores independence between calls — a grader who has seen no other pair cannot carry a cracked signature into the next one — at the cost of needing many more graders for the same number of observations.
open_questions: how many graders per round to get a usable confidence interval near 50%
whether 'fresh context' is achievable for a grader who has ever seen this project's output
what the per-pair difficulty spread is, which the pooled protocol has never measured because it never had independent trials
